 Here are the Upper West Side Street Closures to Know About on Marathon Sunday
 October 30, 2026 | 11:05 AM 
 in 
 NEWS 
 23 
 Runners in the New York City Marathon. Photo by Sam Gross. 
 By Gus Saltonstall 
 The New York City Marathon will happen on Sunday, which means there will be lots of street closures on the Upper West Side.
 Marathon Sunday is a day to celebrate athletic achievement, but it is also a day not to travel more than you need, especially if you’re trying to get across town.
 The race begins at 8 a.m. with the Men’s Wheelchair Division. Since the marathon ends in Central Park, the Upper West Side is also where the “Family Reunion” areas are set up, which help runners find their loved ones after the race is over. This means our neighborhood has a few more street closures than most.
 Here are the Upper West Side street closures related to the New York City Marathon to know about, including in Central Park.
 Central Park South from Fifth to Eighth Avenue: Saturday, October 31 from 8 a.m. to 10:30 a.m.
 Central Park East Drive: Saturday, October 31 through Sunday, November 1
 Central Park West Drive: Saturday, October 31 through Sunday, November 1
 Central Park Center Drive: Saturday, October 31 through Sunday, November 1
 65th Street Traverse: Sunday, November 1 from midnight through 9:30 p.m.
 79th Street Traverse: Sunday, November 1 from midnight through 9:30 p.m.
 96th Street Traverse: Sunday, November 1 from 9 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
 Central Park West from Columbus Circle to 81st Street: Sunday, November 1 from midnight through 10:30 p.m.
 Central Park West from 77th to 86th streets: Sunday, November 1 from 5 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
 Broadway from 59th to 65th streets: Sunday, November 1 from 9:30 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
 Central Park West from 59th to 77th streets: Sunday, November 1 from 5 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
 Columbus Avenue from 59th to 77th streets: Sunday, November 1 from 6 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
 Broadway from 59th to 77th streets: Sunday, November 1 from 6 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.
 Central Park South from Fifth Avenue to Columbus Circle: Sunday, November 1 from 8:30 a.m. to 6:30 p.m.
 Family Reunion Zone 
 West 69th through 71st streets between Columbus and Central Park West from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. on Sunday.
 And here is where you can’t park on the Upper West Side in the lead-up and on the day of the New York City Marathon.
 Central Park West from 60th to 66th streets: Saturday, October 31 through Sunday, November 1.
 Central Park West from 74th to 96th streets: Saturday, October 31 through Sunday, November 1.
 Central Park West to Broadway from 61st to 77th streets: Saturday, October 31 through Sunday, November 1.

 I absolutely love marathon weekend. Even the preparations excite me – the flags of the world, the energy, the excitement building throughout the city.
 But there’s a huge trade-off: the street closures. They cause enormous inconvenience to many people who need to get around that day. I’ve been late to countless events on marathon weekends, even after allowing plenty of extra time. It’s understandable, and something we can live with for a couple of days, but we have to recognize that for some, it’s not just a minor inconvenience. It’s a major disruption.
 Cheering not for the marathon itself but for the actual street closures, just because some transplants want to live in their car-free utopia, is pathological.
